This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

AI-assisted PRs must be accountable and verifiable. Show that the work is not duplicated, name the production invariant being changed, and provide real evidence: production E2E for features and fixes, same-context A/B for performance, and model evals for output or accuracy changes. Every changed file must serve that invariant; remove unrelated cleanup, thin wrappers, generated scaffolding, and mock or source-text tests presented as production evidence.

# Team Documentation Workflow

Collaboration centered on the `docs/` directory.

## Knowledge Architecture (domain-axis)

Docs are organized by what they're *about*, not by lifecycle stage. A doc's freshness lives in its TL;DR (and `Last touched:` for active areas) — not by which directory it sits in. Completed work stays co-located with its domain. There is no `archives/` directory — if a doc no longer earns its keep, delete it; if a lasting lesson hides inside it, lift that lesson into `lessons/` first, then delete.

```
docs/
├── index.md           # Routing table — every doc must be listed here
├── roadmap/           # Strategic plans, quarterly direction, milestones
├── models/<line>/     # Per-model living docs (qwen3, qwen35, kimi-k2, ...)
│                      # — design, accuracy, perf, refactor records, gotchas
├── subsystems/<area>/ # Cross-cutting components (runtime, scheduler, frontend, kernels)
├── playbooks/         # Reusable how-to: benching, profiling, accuracy, onboarding
├── lessons/           # Tribal knowledge from research / other projects
├── benchmarks/        # Standalone benchmark snapshots and eval reports
├── conventions/       # Ongoing standards (bench regression, coding style)
└── private/           # Local-only notes (gitignored)
```

Classification rule at capture time:
- Is it tied to a specific model? → `models/<line>/`
- A specific subsystem? → `subsystems/<area>/`
- Reusable how-to applicable across models? → `playbooks/`
- Lasting lesson from elsewhere (other repo, research, postmortem)? → `lessons/`
- Snapshot of measurement, not a doc that evolves? → `benchmarks/`
- Strategic / cross-cutting plan? → `roadmap/`

If you can't pick one, the doc probably needs splitting.

## Documentation Style

- Docs cover what `--help` and code can't: pitfalls, diagnostic paths, decision context. Don't restate CLI reference.
- Every command in a doc must be run and verified before committing. Unverified commands are technical debt.
- The only required header is a one-line **TL;DR**. Keep it true; that's the contract.
- For `models/<line>/` and `subsystems/<area>/` docs, add `Last touched: YYYY-MM` and bump it when you do meaningful work on the doc (not for typo fixes). The date is a fact, not a judgement — readers infer freshness themselves.
- `playbooks/`, `lessons/`, `conventions/`, `roadmap/`, `benchmarks/`, `archives/` don't need a freshness stamp. They're either timeless until disproven, or self-dated, or explicitly inert.
- No `Status:` enum. Enum fields go stale exactly when you need them most.

## index.md Drift Policy

`index.md` is a routing table with a scanning-friendly TL;DR column. It is *allowed to drift* from the TL;DR inside each doc — the doc body is authoritative. Update `index.md` when you create or delete a doc, or when the existing TL;DR is so wrong it actively misleads. Don't churn it on every doc edit.

## Core Principles (CODE)

Documentation exists to advance work, not to hoard information. Four steps when handling information:

1. **Capture**: Only record what materially advances the project. When in doubt, leave it out.
2. **Organize**: Action-oriented. Resist the urge to organize for organization's sake — structure should be just enough.
3. **Distill**: Refactor over append. When you learn something new or hit a pitfall, integrate it into the document body — don't pile a changelog at the bottom.
4. **Express**: Every document must point to a next step. Split unwieldy documents proactively. Active documents must note the current blocker or next action.

## Collaboration Lifecycle

**Sync**

At the start of each session, you must read `index.md` and load the documents needed for the task at hand.

**Execute**
- Update relevant documents as you go. When a new problem or idea arises, create a document in the appropriate domain directory (see classification rule above).
- Record *why* a decision was made, not just *what* was done.

**Commit**

When a session wraps up:
- Update the TL;DR (and `Last touched`, where applicable) at the top of each modified document.
- Update `index.md` only when you created or deleted a doc, or when its TL;DR row is now misleading (see Drift Policy above).

> **TL;DR:** the kernel_lab fp8 blockwise GEMM experiment line ships 8 units: the production CUTLASS wide route `fp8_gemm.{q_b,o_proj,shared_gate_up,shared_down}` (`glm52_fp8_groupwise_gemm_sm100_cuda`, sm_100a-family only; GB300 sm_103 baselines at rows=64 are 19.77 / 55.77 / 24.03 / 12.92 us, check rel_l2 <= 9.1e-5) plus the CuTe DSL tcgen05 lab line `fp8_gemm_dsl_tc.*` (TMA + tcgen05.mma + TMEM block accumulator + software blockscale, per-shape tile-N/split-K). The DSL variant passes 28/28 on GB300 (rows axis {4..96}, rel_l2 <= 9.1e-5, SASS-audited genuine tcgen05) and beats the CUTLASS baseline on all four shapes: **1.37–1.97x** at rows=64 (best 9.45us / shared_down; tuning round 2 — tile-N/split-K against CTA starvation — adds o_proj −32%, gate_up −40%, down −21%) and **1.34–1.76x** at rows=96 (two M tiles, own `TILE_CFG_MULTI_M` regime). The win survives cold-L2 / CUDA-graph rechecks. Production integration shipped (#835 + #845): build-time `export_to_c` AOT dispatched inside `glm52_fp8_groupwise_gemm_sm100_offset_launch` for the wide-route decode buckets 16–96, measured −8.7~−9.9% whole-step p50 in the wide regime on the ep4 step bench.
>
> **Last touched:** 2026-08

## What this line ships

- **Harness core** (`pegainfer-glm52/benches/kernel_lab/`): manifest-driven registry (the manifest IS the behavior domain — delete a TOML and the unit is gone, no list code to touch), a ctypes loader (dlopens `target/release/libglm52_kernel_lab.so` with `RTLD_LAZY`; DeepEP shim NCCL symbols stay unresolved in the .so and these units never call into them), timing (torch.cuda.Event warm protocol + quack-style `--cold-l2` buffer rotation; cold is mutually exclusive with `--save` to protect ledger comparability), and a ledger (`baselines/<unit>.json` bucketed by `(shape, arch)` — numbers never migrate across arch buckets by contract).
- **Build chain**: with `PEGAINFER_KERNEL_LAB=1`, `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` `nvcc -shared`-links the *same objects and same nvcc flags* as the production static archive into `libglm52_kernel_lab.so` and copies it to `target/<profile>/`; without the env var a default build runs zero extra commands and zero extra link lines.
- **Units**: `fp8_gemm.*` x4 (ctypes straight to the production CUTLASS symbol) + `fp8_gemm_dsl_tc.*` x4 (`capability.python_native` Python JIT units; needs the `.venv`'s `nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.0`). Input pairs are fully same-source across both families (`make_inputs` delegates to fp8_gemm_groupwise: act gets the production per-token-group quantization, weight the 128x128 block quantization recipe, both e4m3 + plain f32 scales, ue8m0 off), one torch reference, one rel_l2 <= 0.02 gate.

- **Tests**: `pegainfer-glm52/benches/tests/` CPU-only pytest (never imports torch): registry/manifest/schema invariants, fp8 unit metadata vs production anchors (`whitelisted_linear_shape` / `FP8_GEMM_WORKSPACE_BYTES` / the `extern "C"` signature), and a latch test for the tcgen05 gating keys.

| Unit (n x k) | us | Note |
|---|---|---|
| fp8_gemm.q_b (16384x2048) | 19.77 | 128 128-N CTAs, SMs nearly fed |
| fp8_gemm.o_proj (6144x16384) | 55.77 | |
| fp8_gemm.shared_gate_up (4096x6144) | 24.03 | only 32 CTAs, CTA-starved |
| fp8_gemm.shared_down (6144x2048) | 12.92 | 48 CTAs |

1	//! Shared GLM5.2 fp8 block-scaled projection primitives (decode, row-batched).
2	//!
3	//! Every dense/attention/expert projection in GLM5.2 is fp8 e4m3 with a per-128
4	//! block `weight_scale_inv`. At m=1 the projection is a weight-only GEMV: the
5	//! bf16 activation is read directly and the fp8 weight is block-scale dequanted
6	//! on the fly (`csrc/glm52/glm52_moe_gemv.cu`) — no activation quant, no TMA
7	//! scale relayout, one kernel instead of three, and weight-memory-bound instead
8	//! of the TRTLLM CUTLASS M-tile padding 1→64. MLA, the dense MLP, and the MoE
9	//! shared expert all share these helpers; only the EP8 routed-expert chain
10	//! (multi-row) stays on the grouped CUTLASS path.

160	/// OCP `float8_e4m3fn` decode (bias 7, no inf; subnormals supported). Used by the
161	/// host-side dequant paths (kv_b absorb factors), not the GPU kernels.
162	pub(crate) fn e4m3_to_f32(b: u8) -> f32 {
163	    let sign = if (b >> 7) & 1 == 1 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 };
164	    let e = ((b >> 3) & 0xF) as i32;
165	    let m = (b & 0x7) as f32;
166	    let mag = if e == 0 {
167	        2f32.powi(-6) * (m / 8.0)
168	    } else {
169	        2f32.powi(e - 7) * (1.0 + m / 8.0)
170	    };
171	    sign * mag
172	}

174	pub(crate) fn bytes_to_f32(b: &[u8]) -> Vec<f32> {
175	    b.as_chunks::<4>()
176	        .0
177	        .iter()
178	        .map(|c| f32::from_le_bytes(*c))
179	        .collect()
180	}

202	        ensure!(
203	            b.weight.len() == b.n * b.k,

209	            b.scale.len() == b.n.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK) * b.k.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK) * 4,

227	    /// Wrap already-resident GPU buffers (the production loader path), moving them
228	    /// in with no copy. `weight` is the fp8 `[n,k]` e4m3 bytes, `scale` the f32
229	    /// `weight_scale_inv` (`[n/128, k/128]`) kept as raw `u8`. Same validation as
230	    /// `upload`, so a packaging drift crashes here, not in the kernel.
231	    pub(crate) fn from_device(
232	        weight: CudaSlice<u8>,
233	        scale: CudaSlice<u8>,
234	        n: usize,
235	        k: usize,
236	    ) -> Result<Self> {
237	        ensure!(
238	            weight.len() == n * k,
239	            "GLM5.2 proj weight bytes {} != n*k {}",
240	            weight.len(),
241	            n * k
242	        );
243	        ensure!(
244	            scale.len() == n.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK) * k.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK) * 4,
245	            "GLM5.2 proj scale bytes {} unexpected for [{n},{k}]",
246	            scale.len()
247	        );
248	        Ok(Self {
249	            weight,
250	            scale,
251	            n,
252	            k,
253	        })
254	    }

257	impl ProjWeight {
258	    /// n-side (output-row) shard: rows `[row_start, row_start + rows)` as a
259	    /// fresh projection. Contiguous device copies. Both bounds must sit on
260	    /// the 128-row scale-block grid — the per-block `weight_scale_inv` rows
261	    /// travel with their weight rows (attention-TP head shards: q_b 8 heads
262	    /// x 256 = 2048 rows, indexer wq_b 4 x 128 = 512, both aligned).
263	    pub(crate) fn slice_rows(
264	        &self,
265	        ctx: &DeviceContext,
266	        row_start: usize,
267	        rows: usize,
268	    ) -> Result<ProjWeight> {
269	        ensure!(
270	            row_start.is_multiple_of(FP8_BLOCK) && rows.is_multiple_of(FP8_BLOCK),
271	            "GLM5.2 proj row slice [{row_start}, +{rows}) off the {FP8_BLOCK}-row scale grid"
272	        );
273	        ensure!(
274	            row_start + rows <= self.n,
275	            "GLM5.2 proj row slice [{row_start}, +{rows}) exceeds n {}",
276	            self.n
277	        );
278	        let mut weight = ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<u8>(rows * self.k)?;
279	        ctx.stream.memcpy_dtod(
280	            &self
281	                .weight
282	                .slice(row_start * self.k..(row_start + rows) * self.k),
283	            &mut weight,
284	        )?;
285	        let scale_cols = self.k.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK);
286	        let mut scale = ctx
287	            .stream
288	            .alloc_zeros::<u8>((rows / FP8_BLOCK) * scale_cols * 4)?;
289	        ctx.stream.memcpy_dtod(
290	            &self.scale.slice(
291	                (row_start / FP8_BLOCK) * scale_cols * 4
292	                    ..((row_start + rows) / FP8_BLOCK) * scale_cols * 4,
293	            ),
294	            &mut scale,
295	        )?;
296	        ProjWeight::from_device(weight, scale, rows, self.k)
297	    }
298	
299	    /// k-side (input-column) shard: columns `[col_start, col_start + cols)`
300	    /// of every row (attention-TP o_proj, whose INPUT is head-major). The
301	    /// gather is strided, so it bounces through the host once — load-time
302	    /// only. Bounds must sit on the 128-column scale-block grid.
303	    pub(crate) fn slice_cols(
304	        &self,
305	        ctx: &DeviceContext,
306	        col_start: usize,
307	        cols: usize,
308	    ) -> Result<ProjWeight> {
309	        ensure!(
310	            col_start.is_multiple_of(FP8_BLOCK) && cols.is_multiple_of(FP8_BLOCK),
311	            "GLM5.2 proj col slice [{col_start}, +{cols}) off the {FP8_BLOCK}-col scale grid"
312	        );
313	        ensure!(
314	            col_start + cols <= self.k,
315	            "GLM5.2 proj col slice [{col_start}, +{cols}) exceeds k {}",
316	            self.k
317	        );
318	        let full_w = ctx.stream.clone_dtoh(&self.weight)?;
319	        let mut w_host = vec![0u8; self.n * cols];
320	        for row in 0..self.n {
321	            w_host[row * cols..(row + 1) * cols].copy_from_slice(
322	                &full_w[row * self.k + col_start..row * self.k + col_start + cols],
323	            );
324	        }
325	        let full_s = ctx.stream.clone_dtoh(&self.scale)?;
326	        let scale_rows = self.n.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK);
327	        let scale_cols = self.k.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK);
328	        let sliced_cols = cols / FP8_BLOCK;
329	        let col_block = col_start / FP8_BLOCK;
330	        let mut s_host = vec![0u8; scale_rows * sliced_cols * 4];
331	        for row in 0..scale_rows {
332	            let src = (row * scale_cols + col_block) * 4;
333	            s_host[row * sliced_cols * 4..(row + 1) * sliced_cols * 4]
334	                .copy_from_slice(&full_s[src..src + sliced_cols * 4]);
335	        }
336	        let mut weight = ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<u8>(w_host.len())?;
337	        ctx.stream.memcpy_htod(&w_host, &mut weight)?;
338	        let mut scale = ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<u8>(s_host.len())?;
339	        ctx.stream.memcpy_htod(&s_host, &mut scale)?;
340	        ProjWeight::from_device(weight, scale, self.n, cols)
341	    }
342	}

344	/// Pack two fp8 projections that share the same input into one `[a.n + b.n, k]`
345	/// projection (weight bytes and per-128-block scale rows concatenated along n).
346	/// Requires `a.n` to be a multiple of 128 so `b`'s scale rows stay aligned to
347	/// the packed row/128 grid. Clients: gate|up (a single GEMV writes the
348	/// `[gate | up]` layout the SwiGLU consumes) and the MLA q_a|kv_a horizontal
349	/// pack (`mla_front::pack_qa_kva`).
350	pub(crate) fn pack_proj_pair(
351	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
352	    a: &ProjWeight,
353	    b: &ProjWeight,
354	) -> Result<ProjWeight> {
355	    ensure!(
356	        a.k == b.k,
357	        "GLM5.2 proj pack k mismatch: {} vs {}",
358	        a.k,
359	        b.k
360	    );
361	    ensure!(
362	        a.n.is_multiple_of(FP8_BLOCK),
363	        "GLM5.2 proj pack first n {} not a multiple of {FP8_BLOCK}",
364	        a.n
365	    );
366	    let n = a.n + b.n;
367	    let mut weight = ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<u8>(n * a.k)?;
368	    ctx.stream
369	        .memcpy_dtod(&a.weight, &mut weight.slice_mut(0..a.n * a.k))?;
370	    ctx.stream
371	        .memcpy_dtod(&b.weight, &mut weight.slice_mut(a.n * a.k..n * a.k))?;
372	    let scale_cols = a.k.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK);
373	    let a_scale_len = (a.n / FP8_BLOCK) * scale_cols * 4;
374	    let b_scale_len = b.n.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK) * scale_cols * 4;
375	    let mut scale = ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<u8>(a_scale_len + b_scale_len)?;
376	    ctx.stream
377	        .memcpy_dtod(&a.scale, &mut scale.slice_mut(0..a_scale_len))?;
378	    ctx.stream.memcpy_dtod(
379	        &b.scale,
380	        &mut scale.slice_mut(a_scale_len..a_scale_len + b_scale_len),
381	    )?;
382	    ProjWeight::from_device(weight, scale, n, a.k)
383	}

385	/// One fp8 projection into a pre-allocated output: weight-only GEMV of `rows`
386	/// bf16 activation rows against the fp8 `[n,k]` weight, block scale dequanted
387	/// on the fly. rows > 1 runs a weight-stationary batched kernel — the weight
388	/// is still read once. rows 1/2 keep bit-stable CUDA-core paths; rows 4/8
389	/// dispatch to a tensor-core mma path on winning shapes (deterministic per
390	/// bucket, not bit-identical to rows=1 — cross-bucket FP divergence is the
391	/// accepted whole-step contract; numerics notes in glm52_moe_gemv.cu).

401	        input.len() >= rows * w.k,

405	    );
406	    glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_launch(

476	    // instead. Same per-scratch ownership discipline as `gemv_partial`.
477	    wide: Option<Glm52Fp8GemmScratch>,
478	}

480	impl Glm52MlpScratch {
481	    pub(crate) fn new(ctx: &DeviceContext, intermediate: usize, rows: usize) -> Result<Self> {
482	        ensure!(
483	            intermediate.is_multiple_of(FP8_BLOCK),
484	            "GLM5.2 fp8_mlp intermediate {intermediate} not a multiple of {FP8_BLOCK}"
485	        );
486	        ensure!(rows > 0, "GLM5.2 fp8_mlp scratch needs positive rows");
487	        Ok(Self {
488	            intermediate,
489	            rows,
490	            gate_up: ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<bf16>(rows * 2 * intermediate)?,
491	            silu_out: ctx.stream.alloc_zeros::<bf16>(rows * intermediate)?,
492	            gemv_partial: ctx
493	                .stream
494	                .alloc_zeros::<f32>(rows * GLM52_GEMV_MMA_SCRATCH_FLOATS_PER_ROW)?,
495	            wide: (rows > FP8_GEMV_MAX_ROWS)
496	                .then(|| {
497	                    // gate|up consumes hidden (k = 6144); down consumes the
498	                    // intermediate — one scratch covers both legs.
499	                    Glm52Fp8GemmScratch::new(
500	                        ctx,
501	                        rows.next_multiple_of(4),
502	                        crate::config::GLM52_HIDDEN.max(intermediate),
503	                    )
504	                })
505	                .transpose()?,
506	        })
507	    }
508	}
509	
510	/// A plain fp8 SwiGLU MLP over the scratch's `rows` tokens into a
511	/// pre-allocated output: `down(silu(gate(h)) * up(h))` with the gate|up
512	/// projections PACKED into one `[2*intermediate, k]` weight (see
513	/// [`pack_proj_pair`]) — a single GEMV writes the `[gate | up]` layout the
514	/// SwiGLU consumes, no concat copies. `out` is `[rows, down.n]` bf16.
515	pub(crate) fn fp8_mlp_into(
516	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
517	    gate_up: &ProjWeight,
518	    down: &ProjWeight,
519	    input: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
520	    s: &mut Glm52MlpScratch,
521	    out: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
522	) -> Result<()> {
523	    // gate_up/down internal consistency is pinned where the weight bundles
524	    // are built (`Glm52DenseMlpWeights` / `Glm52MoeSharedExpert` check exact
525	    // shapes); the scratch pairing is the one cross-object join this call
526	    // introduces, so it is the one thing validated here.
527	    let intermediate = gate_up.n / 2;
528	    ensure!(
529	        s.intermediate == intermediate,
530	        "GLM5.2 fp8_mlp scratch sized for intermediate {} but weights have {intermediate}",
531	        s.intermediate
532	    );
533	    // Wide buckets (#812): both projections run the fp8 GEMM; the SwiGLU is
534	    // the standalone bf16 kernel (no partials to absorb).
535	    if let Some(wide) = s.wide.as_mut() {
536	        fp8_linear_large_m_into(ctx, gate_up, s.rows, input, wide, &mut s.gate_up)?;
537	        glm52_silu_and_mul_bf16_launch(ctx, s.rows, intermediate, &s.gate_up, &mut s.silu_out)?;
538	        return fp8_linear_large_m_into(ctx, down, s.rows, &s.silu_out, wide, out);
539	    }
540	    // The gate|up projection stops at its f32 k-slice partials when the
541	    // (rows, shape) routes to the mma path, and the SwiGLU absorbs the
542	    // fixed-order reduce (one launch instead of two, bit-identical); the
543	    // register-tile rows keep the bf16 GEMV -> standalone SwiGLU pair.
544	    let ksplit = glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_partials_launch(
545	        ctx,
546	        s.rows,
547	        gate_up.n,
548	        gate_up.k,
549	        input,
550	        &gate_up.weight,
551	        &gate_up.scale,
552	        &mut s.gemv_partial,
553	        &mut s.gate_up,
554	    )?;
555	    if ksplit == 0 {
556	        // bf16 SwiGLU (no route weight, no activation quant) -> bf16 down input.
557	        glm52_silu_and_mul_bf16_launch(ctx, s.rows, intermediate, &s.gate_up, &mut s.silu_out)?;
558	    } else {
559	        glm52_gemv_reduce_silu_mul_launch(
560	            ctx,
561	            s.rows,
562	            intermediate,
563	            ksplit,
564	            &s.gemv_partial,
565	            &mut s.silu_out,
566	        )?;
567	    }
568	    fp8_linear_into(
569	        ctx,
570	        down,
571	        s.rows,
572	        &s.silu_out,
573	        Some(&mut s.gemv_partial),
574	        out,
575	    )
576	}

702	        let scale_rows = n / FP8_BLOCK;
703	        let scale_cols = k / FP8_BLOCK;
704	        let scale: Vec<u8> = (0..scale_rows * scale_cols * 4)
705	            .map(|i| (i * 13 % 241) as u8)
706	            .collect();
707	        let proj = ProjWeight::upload(

711	                scale: &scale,

718	        let rows = proj.slice_rows(&ctx, FP8_BLOCK, 2 * FP8_BLOCK)?;
719	        assert_eq!((rows.n, rows.k), (2 * FP8_BLOCK, k));

730	        let cols = proj.slice_cols(&ctx, FP8_BLOCK, FP8_BLOCK)?;

732	        let mut w_ref = Vec::with_capacity(n * FP8_BLOCK);
733	        let mut s_ref = Vec::with_capacity(scale_rows * 4);

# 项目学习手册·单篇讲义生成 Worker

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

---

## 代码实践要求

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

实践优先从以下位置寻找依据：

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。
- 根据测试断言理解行为。
- 修改局部参数并说明应该观察什么。
- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. 1	//! GLM5.2 weight-only FP8 GEMV and bf16 SwiGLU helpers used by dense,
2	//! attention, indexer, and shared-expert projections.
3	
4	use anyhow::Result;
5	use anyhow::anyhow;
6	use anyhow::ensure;
7	use cudarc::driver::CudaSlice;
8	use cudarc::driver::DevicePtr;
9	use cudarc::driver::DevicePtrMut;
10	use half::bf16;
11	
12	use crate::ffi;
13	use crate::tensor::DeviceContext;
14	
15	const FP8_BLOCK: usize = 128;
16	
17	/// Plain `SiLU(gate) * up` over `[rows, 2*inter]` into `[rows, inter]`.
18	pub fn glm52_silu_and_mul_bf16_launch(
19	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
20	    rows: usize,
21	    inter: usize,
22	    input: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
23	    output: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
24	) -> Result<()> {
25	    ensure!(
26	        rows > 0 && inter > 0,
27	        "GLM5.2 SiLU needs positive rows/inter, got {rows}/{inter}"
28	    );
29	    ensure!(
30	        input.len() >= rows * 2 * inter && output.len() >= rows * inter,
31	        "GLM5.2 SiLU buffers too small: in {}, out {}",
32	        input.len(),
33	        output.len()
34	    );
35	    let (in_ptr, _i) = input.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
36	    let (out_ptr, _o) = output.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
37	    unsafe {
38	        ffi::glm52_silu_and_mul_bf16_cuda(
39	            in_ptr as *const ffi::Half,
40	            out_ptr as *mut ffi::Half,
41	            rows as i32,
42	            inter as i32,
43	            ctx.stream.cu_stream(),
44	        )
45	    }
46	    .result()
47	    .map_err(|err| anyhow!("GLM5.2 SiLU launch failed: {err}"))
48	}
49	
50	/// f32 partial-scratch floats PER ROW the tensor-core batched GEMV path can
51	/// need: max ksplit (16) × max whitelisted n (dense gate|up 24576). Callers
52	/// size their buffer as `rows * GLM52_GEMV_MMA_SCRATCH_FLOATS_PER_ROW` — one
53	/// constant instead of mirroring the CUDA-side per-shape config table; the
54	/// launcher still guards the exact requirement and rejects a short buffer.
55	/// (The Blackwell table's larger splits only apply to small n — 48 × 2048
56	/// stays well inside this budget; the CUDA-side guard is the invariant.)
57	pub const GLM52_GEMV_MMA_SCRATCH_FLOATS_PER_ROW: usize = 16 * 24576;
58	
59	/// Fused fixed-order k-slice reduce + `SiLU(gate) * up`: consumes the f32
60	/// partials a [`glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_partials_launch`] left in scratch
61	/// for a packed gate|up projection. Bit-identical to the standalone
62	/// reduce -> silu pair (both sums round to bf16 before the SiLU math).
63	pub fn glm52_gemv_reduce_silu_mul_launch(
64	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
65	    rows: usize,
66	    inter: usize,
67	    ksplit: usize,
68	    partial: &CudaSlice<f32>,
69	    output: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
70	) -> Result<()> {
71	    ensure!(
72	        rows > 0 && inter > 0 && ksplit >= 1,
73	        "GLM5.2 reduce-SiLU needs positive rows/inter/ksplit, got {rows}/{inter}/{ksplit}"
74	    );
75	    ensure!(
76	        partial.len() >= ksplit * rows * 2 * inter && output.len() >= rows * inter,
77	        "GLM5.2 reduce-SiLU buffers too small: partial {} (need {}), out {} (need {})",
78	        partial.len(),
79	        ksplit * rows * 2 * inter,
80	        output.len(),
81	        rows * inter
82	    );
83	    let (p_ptr, _p) = partial.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
84	    let (out_ptr, _o) = output.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
85	    unsafe {
86	        ffi::glm52_gemv_reduce_silu_mul_cuda(
87	            p_ptr as *const f32,
88	            out_ptr as *mut ffi::Half,
89	            rows as i32,
90	            inter as i32,
91	            ksplit as i32,
92	            ctx.stream.cu_stream(),
93	        )
94	    }
95	    .result()
96	    .map_err(|err| anyhow!("GLM5.2 reduce-SiLU launch failed: {err}"))
97	}
98	
99	/// Fixed-order k-slice reduce for a horizontally packed projection pair:
100	/// de-interleaves the packed `[ksplit, rows, n_a + n_b]` partials into the two
101	/// compact per-projection bf16 outputs. Same summation order and rounding as
102	/// the plain reduce.
103	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
104	pub fn glm52_gemv_split_reduce_launch(
105	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
106	    rows: usize,
107	    n_a: usize,
108	    n_b: usize,
109	    ksplit: usize,
110	    partial: &CudaSlice<f32>,
111	    out_a: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
112	    out_b: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
113	) -> Result<()> {
114	    ensure!(
115	        rows > 0 && n_a > 0 && n_b > 0 && ksplit >= 1,
116	        "GLM5.2 split-reduce needs positive rows/n_a/n_b/ksplit, got {rows}/{n_a}/{n_b}/{ksplit}"
117	    );
118	    ensure!(
119	        partial.len() >= ksplit * rows * (n_a + n_b)
120	            && out_a.len() >= rows * n_a
121	            && out_b.len() >= rows * n_b,
122	        "GLM5.2 split-reduce buffers too small: partial {} (need {}), out_a {} (need {}), out_b {} (need {})",
123	        partial.len(),
124	        ksplit * rows * (n_a + n_b),
125	        out_a.len(),
126	        rows * n_a,
127	        out_b.len(),
128	        rows * n_b
129	    );
130	    let (p_ptr, _p) = partial.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
131	    let (a_ptr, _a) = out_a.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
132	    let (b_ptr, _b) = out_b.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
133	    unsafe {
134	        ffi::glm52_gemv_split_reduce_cuda(
135	            p_ptr as *const f32,
136	            a_ptr as *mut ffi::Half,
137	            b_ptr as *mut ffi::Half,
138	            rows as i32,
139	            n_a as i32,
140	            n_b as i32,
141	            ksplit as i32,
142	            ctx.stream.cu_stream(),
143	        )
144	    }
145	    .result()
146	    .map_err(|err| anyhow!("GLM5.2 split-reduce launch failed: {err}"))
147	}
148	
149	/// Whether the batched GEMV mma table has an entry for (batch, n, k) — the
150	/// gate for routing a horizontally packed projection through one batched
151	/// launch. Without an entry the packed launch would take the register tile
152	/// and write an interleaved layout no consumer understands, so callers fall
153	/// back to separate per-projection launches.
154	pub fn glm52_gemv_mma_routes(batch: usize, n: usize, k: usize) -> Result<bool> {
155	    let mut ksplit: i32 = 0;
156	    unsafe { ffi::glm52_gemv_mma_ksplit_cuda(batch as i32, n as i32, k as i32, &raw mut ksplit) }
157	        .result()
158	        .map_err(|err| anyhow!("GLM5.2 mma ksplit query failed: {err}"))?;
159	    Ok(ksplit > 0)
160	}
161	
162	/// Plain weight-only fp8 GEMV (bs=1): `out[n] = deq(weight[n,k]) @ activation[k]`
163	/// with the bf16 activation read directly (no activation quant, no scale
164	/// relayout) and the e4m3 block-scale weight dequanted on the fly. Replaces
165	/// the TRTLLM CUTLASS block-scale GEMM at m=1, where the M-tile pads 1->64 and
166	/// runs compute-bound. `scale_bytes` is the checkpoint `weight_scale_inv`
167	/// (f32 `[ceil(n/128), k/128]`) kept as raw bytes.
168	///
169	/// `scratch` is the caller-owned f32 partial buffer for the rows-4/8
170	/// tensor-core path. Ownership contract: the layer forward overlaps the ctx
171	/// and aux streams, so a scratch buffer must belong to exactly one launch
172	/// stream — every scratch struct owns its own. Pass `None` only on rows ≤ 2
173	/// paths; an mma-routed launch without a buffer fails loudly.
174	pub fn glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_launch(
175	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
176	    rows: usize,
177	    n: usize,
178	    k: usize,
179	    activation: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
180	    weight: &CudaSlice<u8>,
181	    scale_bytes: &CudaSlice<u8>,
182	    scratch: Option<&mut CudaSlice<f32>>,
183	    out: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
184	) -> Result<()> {
185	    gemv_batched_launch(
186	        ctx,
187	        rows,
188	        n,
189	        k,
190	        activation,
191	        weight,
192	        scale_bytes,
193	        scratch,
194	        out,
195	        None,
196	    )
197	}
198	
199	/// Partials-producing twin of [`glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_launch`]: when the
200	/// (batch, shape) routes to the tensor-core mma path, the launch stops at the
201	/// f32 k-slice partials in `scratch` and returns the split factor (`out` is
202	/// untouched); otherwise it behaves exactly like the plain launch and returns
203	/// 0. Callers pair a non-zero return with a fused reduce consumer.
204	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
205	pub fn glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_partials_launch(
206	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
207	    rows: usize,
208	    n: usize,
209	    k: usize,
210	    activation: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
211	    weight: &CudaSlice<u8>,
212	    scale_bytes: &CudaSlice<u8>,
213	    scratch: &mut CudaSlice<f32>,
214	    out: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
215	) -> Result<usize> {
216	    let mut ksplit: i32 = 0;
217	    gemv_batched_launch(
218	        ctx,
219	        rows,
220	        n,
221	        k,
222	        activation,
223	        weight,
224	        scale_bytes,
225	        Some(scratch),
226	        out,
227	        Some(&mut ksplit),
228	    )?;
229	    Ok(ksplit as usize)
230	}
231	
232	/// Shared body of the two entry points above: validation, pointer extraction,
233	/// and the FFI call (plain when `ksplit_out` is `None`, partials otherwise).
234	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
235	fn gemv_batched_launch(
236	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
237	    rows: usize,
238	    n: usize,
239	    k: usize,
240	    activation: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
241	    weight: &CudaSlice<u8>,
242	    scale_bytes: &CudaSlice<u8>,
243	    scratch: Option<&mut CudaSlice<f32>>,
244	    out: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
245	    ksplit_out: Option<&mut i32>,
246	) -> Result<()> {
247	    ensure!(
248	        rows > 0 && n > 0 && k > 0,
249	        "GLM5.2 linear GEMV needs positive rows/n/k, got {rows}/{n}/{k}"
250	    );
251	    let scale_len = n.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK) * k.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK) * 4;
252	    ensure!(
253	        weight.len() >= n * k
254	            && scale_bytes.len() >= scale_len
255	            && activation.len() >= rows * k
256	            && out.len() >= rows * n,
257	        "GLM5.2 linear GEMV buffers too small: w {} (need {}), scale {} (need {scale_len}), act {} (need {}), out {} (need {})",
258	        weight.len(),
259	        n * k,
260	        scale_bytes.len(),
261	        activation.len(),
262	        rows * k,
263	        out.len(),
264	        rows * n
265	    );
266	    ensure!(
267	        ksplit_out.is_none() || rows <= 48,
268	        "GLM5.2 linear GEMV partials path is not token-split past 48 rows (got {rows})"
269	    );
270	    let (act_ptr, _a) = activation.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
271	    let (w_ptr, _w) = weight.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
272	    let (s_ptr, _s) = scale_bytes.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
273	    let (out_ptr, _o) = out.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
274	    let (scr_ptr, scr_floats, _scr) = match scratch {
275	        Some(buf) => {
276	            let len = buf.len();
277	            let (ptr, guard) = buf.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
278	            (ptr as *mut f32, len, Some(guard))
279	        }
280	        None => (std::ptr::null_mut(), 0, None),
281	    };
282	    // rows == 1 runs the m=1 kernel; rows 2 the bit-parity register tile;
283	    // rows 4/8 the tensor-core mma path on winning shapes (deterministic per
284	    // bucket, not bit-identical to m=1). The CUDA side whitelists the
285	    // supported batches — a drifted GLM52_DECODE_BUCKETS crashes here.
286	    match ksplit_out {
287	        None => {
288	            // 64/96-row buckets (#817) split on the token axis into two
289	            // whitelisted sub-batches — the register tile at those widths
290	            // would spill (the #813 lesson), and the activation/out layouts
291	            // are token-major so the split is a pointer offset.
292	            let halves: &[(usize, usize)] = match rows {
293	                64 => &[(32, 0), (32, 32)],
294	                96 => &[(48, 0), (48, 48)],
295	                _ => &[(rows, 0)],
296	            };
297	            let mut result = cudarc::driver::sys::CUresult::CUDA_SUCCESS;
298	            for &(sub, off) in halves {
299	                result = unsafe {
300	                    ffi::glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_batched_cuda(
301	                        (act_ptr as *const ffi::Half).add(off * k),
302	                        w_ptr as *const u8,
303	                        s_ptr as *const f32,
304	                        (out_ptr as *mut ffi::Half).add(off * n),
305	                        scr_ptr,
306	                        scr_floats,
307	                        sub as i32,
308	                        n as i32,
309	                        k as i32,
310	                        ctx.stream.cu_stream(),
311	                    )
312	                };
313	                if result != cudarc::driver::sys::CUresult::CUDA_SUCCESS {
314	                    break;
315	                }
316	            }
317	            result
318	        }
319	        Some(ksplit) => unsafe {
320	            ffi::glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_partials_cuda(
321	                act_ptr as *const ffi::Half,
322	                w_ptr as *const u8,
323	                s_ptr as *const f32,
324	                out_ptr as *mut ffi::Half,
325	                scr_ptr,
326	                scr_floats,
327	                rows as i32,
328	                n as i32,
329	                k as i32,
330	                ctx.stream.cu_stream(),
331	                ksplit,
332	            )
333	        },
334	    }
335	    .result()
336	    .map_err(|err| anyhow!("GLM5.2 linear GEMV launch failed for rows={rows}, n={n}, k={k}: {err}"))
337	}

339	/// MLA's bs=1 q_a and kv_a projections in one graph node. The two weights and
340	/// outputs remain separate; CUDA concatenates only their block grids.
341	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
342	pub fn glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_pair_launch(
343	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
344	    k: usize,
345	    activation: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
346	    n_a: usize,
347	    weight_a: &CudaSlice<u8>,
348	    scale_a: &CudaSlice<u8>,
349	    out_a: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
350	    n_b: usize,
351	    weight_b: &CudaSlice<u8>,
352	    scale_b: &CudaSlice<u8>,
353	    out_b: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
354	) -> Result<()> {
355	    let scale_len = |n: usize| n.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK) * k.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK) * 4;
356	    ensure!(
357	        k > 0
358	            && activation.len() >= k
359	            && weight_a.len() >= n_a * k
360	            && scale_a.len() >= scale_len(n_a)
361	            && out_a.len() >= n_a
362	            && weight_b.len() >= n_b * k
363	            && scale_b.len() >= scale_len(n_b)
364	            && out_b.len() >= n_b,
365	        "GLM5.2 paired GEMV buffers do not cover [{n_a},{k}] + [{n_b},{k}]"
366	    );
367	    let (act_ptr, _act) = activation.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
368	    let (wa_ptr, _wa) = weight_a.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
369	    let (sa_ptr, _sa) = scale_a.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
370	    let (oa_ptr, _oa) = out_a.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
371	    let (wb_ptr, _wb) = weight_b.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
372	    let (sb_ptr, _sb) = scale_b.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
373	    let (ob_ptr, _ob) = out_b.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
374	    unsafe {
375	        ffi::glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_pair_cuda(
376	            act_ptr as *const ffi::Half,
377	            wa_ptr as *const u8,
378	            sa_ptr as *const f32,
379	            oa_ptr as *mut ffi::Half,
380	            n_a as i32,
381	            wb_ptr as *const u8,
382	            sb_ptr as *const f32,
383	            ob_ptr as *mut ffi::Half,
384	            n_b as i32,
385	            k as i32,
386	            ctx.stream.cu_stream(),
387	        )
388	    }
389	    .result()
390	    .map_err(|err| anyhow!("GLM5.2 paired GEMV launch failed: {err}"))
391	}

73	/// fp8 sparse KV-cache contract. The sm100 decode kernel truncates the stored
74	/// f32 scales to e8m0 (round-toward-zero) for its block-scaled MMA, so a

76	/// f32 scales exactly. Power-of-two scales are exact on both. Use this for
77	/// every write into the 656-byte fp8_ds_mla cache and nowhere else (the MoE
78	/// and dense GEMM activations keep amax/448 scales).

137	/// `row_map` redirects each row to its masked slot (skipping alignment
138	/// gaps), values land in `[groups, masked_cap, width]` and scales in the
139	/// mn-major `[groups, width/128, masked_cap]` layout the masked GEMM's SFA
140	/// descriptor reads. Active-row scales are powers of two; pack them with
141	/// [`glm52_fp8_scale_pack_ue8m0_launch`] before the GEMM.

248	/// Pack power-of-two f32 scales from `[groups, scale_cols, cap]` into the

277	            scale_cols as i32,

287	/// Convert one expert bank in place from arbitrary f32 block scales to the
288	/// power-of-two UE8M0 contract required by the SM100 DeepGEMM kernel, and
289	/// pack those scales into `[groups, k / 512, n]`.
290	pub fn glm52_fp8_weight_ue8m0_prepare_launch(
291	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
292	    groups: usize,
293	    n: usize,
294	    k: usize,
295	    weight: &mut CudaSlice<u8>,
296	    scales: &CudaSlice<f32>,
297	    packed_scales: &mut CudaSlice<i32>,
298	) -> Result<()> {
299	    ensure!(
300	        groups > 0
301	            && n > 0
302	            && n.is_multiple_of(GLM52_MOE_QUANT_GROUP_SIZE)
303	            && k.is_multiple_of(4 * GLM52_MOE_QUANT_GROUP_SIZE),
304	        "GLM5.2 weight UE8M0 prepare needs groups>0, n%128=0, k%512=0; got groups={groups}, n={n}, k={k}"
305	    );
306	    let weight_len = groups * n * k;
307	    let scale_len = groups * (n / GLM52_MOE_QUANT_GROUP_SIZE) * (k / GLM52_MOE_QUANT_GROUP_SIZE);
308	    let packed_len = groups * (k / (4 * GLM52_MOE_QUANT_GROUP_SIZE)) * n;
309	    ensure!(
310	        weight.len() >= weight_len
311	            && scales.len() >= scale_len
312	            && packed_scales.len() >= packed_len,
313	        "GLM5.2 weight UE8M0 buffers too small: weight {}, scales {}, packed {}, need {weight_len}/{scale_len}/{packed_len}",
314	        weight.len(),
315	        scales.len(),
316	        packed_scales.len()
317	    );
318	    let (weight_ptr, _weight_guard) = weight.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
319	    let (scales_ptr, _scales_guard) = scales.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
320	    let (packed_ptr, _packed_guard) = packed_scales.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
321	    let requant = unsafe {
322	        ffi::glm52_fp8_weight_ue8m0_requant_cuda(
323	            weight_ptr as *mut u8,
324	            scales_ptr as *const f32,
325	            groups as i32,
326	            n as i32,
327	            k as i32,
328	            ctx.stream.cu_stream(),
329	        )
330	    };
331	    requant
332	        .result()
333	        .map_err(|err| anyhow!("GLM5.2 weight UE8M0 requant launch failed: {err}"))?;
334	    let pack = unsafe {
335	        ffi::glm52_fp8_weight_scale_pack_ue8m0_cuda(
336	            scales_ptr as *const f32,
337	            packed_ptr as *mut i32,
338	            groups as i32,
339	            n as i32,
340	            k as i32,
341	            ctx.stream.cu_stream(),
342	        )
343	    };
344	    pack.result()
345	        .map_err(|err| anyhow!("GLM5.2 weight UE8M0 scale pack launch failed: {err}"))
346	}

17	/// Plain `SiLU(gate) * up` over `[rows, 2*inter]` into `[rows, inter]`.
18	pub fn glm52_silu_and_mul_bf16_launch(
19	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
20	    rows: usize,
21	    inter: usize,
22	    input: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
23	    output: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
24	) -> Result<()> {
25	    ensure!(
26	        rows > 0 && inter > 0,
27	        "GLM5.2 SiLU needs positive rows/inter, got {rows}/{inter}"
28	    );
29	    ensure!(
30	        input.len() >= rows * 2 * inter && output.len() >= rows * inter,
31	        "GLM5.2 SiLU buffers too small: in {}, out {}",
32	        input.len(),
33	        output.len()
34	    );
35	    let (in_ptr, _i) = input.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
36	    let (out_ptr, _o) = output.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
37	    unsafe {
38	        ffi::glm52_silu_and_mul_bf16_cuda(
39	            in_ptr as *const ffi::Half,
40	            out_ptr as *mut ffi::Half,
41	            rows as i32,
42	            inter as i32,
43	            ctx.stream.cu_stream(),
44	        )
45	    }
46	    .result()
47	    .map_err(|err| anyhow!("GLM5.2 SiLU launch failed: {err}"))

50	/// f32 partial-scratch floats PER ROW the tensor-core batched GEMV path can
51	/// need: max ksplit (16) × max whitelisted n (dense gate|up 24576). Callers
52	/// size their buffer as `rows * GLM52_GEMV_MMA_SCRATCH_FLOATS_PER_ROW` — one
53	/// constant instead of mirroring the CUDA-side per-shape config table; the
54	/// launcher still guards the exact requirement and rejects a short buffer.
55	/// (The Blackwell table's larger splits only apply to small n — 48 × 2048
56	/// stays well inside this budget; the CUDA-side guard is the invariant.)
57	pub const GLM52_GEMV_MMA_SCRATCH_FLOATS_PER_ROW: usize = 16 * 24576;

99	/// Fixed-order k-slice reduce for a horizontally packed projection pair:
100	/// de-interleaves the packed `[ksplit, rows, n_a + n_b]` partials into the two
101	/// compact per-projection bf16 outputs. Same summation order and rounding as
102	/// the plain reduce.
103	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
104	pub fn glm52_gemv_split_reduce_launch(
105	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
106	    rows: usize,
107	    n_a: usize,
108	    n_b: usize,
109	    ksplit: usize,
110	    partial: &CudaSlice<f32>,
111	    out_a: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
112	    out_b: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
113	) -> Result<()> {
114	    ensure!(
115	        rows > 0 && n_a > 0 && n_b > 0 && ksplit >= 1,
116	        "GLM5.2 split-reduce needs positive rows/n_a/n_b/ksplit, got {rows}/{n_a}/{n_b}/{ksplit}"
117	    );
118	    ensure!(
119	        partial.len() >= ksplit * rows * (n_a + n_b)
120	            && out_a.len() >= rows * n_a
121	            && out_b.len() >= rows * n_b,
122	        "GLM5.2 split-reduce buffers too small: partial {} (need {}), out_a {} (need {}), out_b {} (need {})",
123	        partial.len(),

127	        out_b.len(),

131	    let (a_ptr, _a) = out_a.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
132	    let (b_ptr, _b) = out_b.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);

137	            b_ptr as *mut ffi::Half,

139	            n_a as i32,
140	            n_b as i32,
141	            ksplit as i32,

143	        )
144	    }

149	/// Whether the batched GEMV mma table has an entry for (batch, n, k) — the
150	/// gate for routing a horizontally packed projection through one batched
151	/// launch. Without an entry the packed launch would take the register tile
152	/// and write an interleaved layout no consumer understands, so callers fall
153	/// back to separate per-projection launches.
154	pub fn glm52_gemv_mma_routes(batch: usize, n: usize, k: usize) -> Result<bool> {
155	    let mut ksplit: i32 = 0;
156	    unsafe { ffi::glm52_gemv_mma_ksplit_cuda(batch as i32, n as i32, k as i32, &raw mut ksplit) }
157	        .result()
158	        .map_err(|err| anyhow!("GLM5.2 mma ksplit query failed: {err}"))?;
159	    Ok(ksplit > 0)

162	/// Plain weight-only fp8 GEMV (bs=1): `out[n] = deq(weight[n,k]) @ activation[k]`
163	/// with the bf16 activation read directly (no activation quant, no scale
164	/// relayout) and the e4m3 block-scale weight dequanted on the fly. Replaces
165	/// the TRTLLM CUTLASS block-scale GEMM at m=1, where the M-tile pads 1->64 and
166	/// runs compute-bound. `scale_bytes` is the checkpoint `weight_scale_inv`
167	/// (f32 `[ceil(n/128), k/128]`) kept as raw bytes.
168	///
169	/// `scratch` is the caller-owned f32 partial buffer for the rows-4/8
170	/// tensor-core path. Ownership contract: the layer forward overlaps the ctx
171	/// and aux streams, so a scratch buffer must belong to exactly one launch
172	/// stream — every scratch struct owns its own. Pass `None` only on rows ≤ 2
173	/// paths; an mma-routed launch without a buffer fails loudly.
174	pub fn glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_launch(
175	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
176	    rows: usize,
177	    n: usize,
178	    k: usize,
179	    activation: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
180	    weight: &CudaSlice<u8>,
181	    scale_bytes: &CudaSlice<u8>,
182	    scratch: Option<&mut CudaSlice<f32>>,
183	    out: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
184	) -> Result<()> {
185	    gemv_batched_launch(
186	        ctx,
187	        rows,
188	        n,
189	        k,
190	        activation,
191	        weight,
192	        scale_bytes,
193	        scratch,
194	        out,
195	        None,
196	    )
197	}

199	/// Partials-producing twin of [`glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_launch`]: when the
200	/// (batch, shape) routes to the tensor-core mma path, the launch stops at the
201	/// f32 k-slice partials in `scratch` and returns the split factor (`out` is
202	/// untouched); otherwise it behaves exactly like the plain launch and returns
203	/// 0. Callers pair a non-zero return with a fused reduce consumer.
204	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
205	pub fn glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_partials_launch(
206	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
207	    rows: usize,
208	    n: usize,
209	    k: usize,
210	    activation: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
211	    weight: &CudaSlice<u8>,
212	    scale_bytes: &CudaSlice<u8>,
213	    scratch: &mut CudaSlice<f32>,
214	    out: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
215	) -> Result<usize> {
216	    let mut ksplit: i32 = 0;
217	    gemv_batched_launch(
218	        ctx,
219	        rows,
220	        n,
221	        k,
222	        activation,
223	        weight,
224	        scale_bytes,
225	        Some(scratch),
226	        out,
227	        Some(&mut ksplit),
228	    )?;
229	    Ok(ksplit as usize)
230	}

232	/// Shared body of the two entry points above: validation, pointer extraction,
233	/// and the FFI call (plain when `ksplit_out` is `None`, partials otherwise).
234	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
235	fn gemv_batched_launch(
236	    ctx: &DeviceContext,
237	    rows: usize,
238	    n: usize,
239	    k: usize,
240	    activation: &CudaSlice<bf16>,
241	    weight: &CudaSlice<u8>,
242	    scale_bytes: &CudaSlice<u8>,
243	    scratch: Option<&mut CudaSlice<f32>>,
244	    out: &mut CudaSlice<bf16>,
245	    ksplit_out: Option<&mut i32>,
246	) -> Result<()> {
247	    ensure!(
248	        rows > 0 && n > 0 && k > 0,
249	        "GLM5.2 linear GEMV needs positive rows/n/k, got {rows}/{n}/{k}"
250	    );
251	    let scale_len = n.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK) * k.div_ceil(FP8_BLOCK) * 4;
252	    ensure!(
253	        weight.len() >= n * k
254	            && scale_bytes.len() >= scale_len
255	            && activation.len() >= rows * k
256	            && out.len() >= rows * n,
257	        "GLM5.2 linear GEMV buffers too small: w {} (need {}), scale {} (need {scale_len}), act {} (need {}), out {} (need {})",
258	        weight.len(),
259	        n * k,
260	        scale_bytes.len(),
261	        activation.len(),
262	        rows * k,
263	        out.len(),
264	        rows * n
265	    );
266	    ensure!(
267	        ksplit_out.is_none() || rows <= 48,
268	        "GLM5.2 linear GEMV partials path is not token-split past 48 rows (got {rows})"
269	    );
270	    let (act_ptr, _a) = activation.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
271	    let (w_ptr, _w) = weight.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
272	    let (s_ptr, _s) = scale_bytes.device_ptr(&ctx.stream);
273	    let (out_ptr, _o) = out.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
274	    let (scr_ptr, scr_floats, _scr) = match scratch {
275	        Some(buf) => {
276	            let len = buf.len();
277	            let (ptr, guard) = buf.device_ptr_mut(&ctx.stream);
278	            (ptr as *mut f32, len, Some(guard))
279	        }
280	        None => (std::ptr::null_mut(), 0, None),
281	    };
282	    // rows == 1 runs the m=1 kernel; rows 2 the bit-parity register tile;
283	    // rows 4/8 the tensor-core mma path on winning shapes (deterministic per
284	    // bucket, not bit-identical to m=1). The CUDA side whitelists the
285	    // supported batches — a drifted GLM52_DECODE_BUCKETS crashes here.
286	    match ksplit_out {
287	        None => {
288	            // 64/96-row buckets (#817) split on the token axis into two
289	            // whitelisted sub-batches — the register tile at those widths
290	            // would spill (the #813 lesson), and the activation/out layouts
291	            // are token-major so the split is a pointer offset.
292	            let halves: &[(usize, usize)] = match rows {
293	                64 => &[(32, 0), (32, 32)],
294	                96 => &[(48, 0), (48, 48)],
295	                _ => &[(rows, 0)],
296	            };
297	            let mut result = cudarc::driver::sys::CUresult::CUDA_SUCCESS;
298	            for &(sub, off) in halves {
299	                result = unsafe {
300	                    ffi::glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_batched_cuda(
301	                        (act_ptr as *const ffi::Half).add(off * k),
302	                        w_ptr as *const u8,
303	                        s_ptr as *const f32,
304	                        (out_ptr as *mut ffi::Half).add(off * n),
305	                        scr_ptr,
306	                        scr_floats,
307	                        sub as i32,
308	                        n as i32,
309	                        k as i32,
310	                        ctx.stream.cu_stream(),
311	                    )
312	                };
313	                if result != cudarc::driver::sys::CUresult::CUDA_SUCCESS {
314	                    break;
315	                }
316	            }
317	            result
318	        }
319	        Some(ksplit) => unsafe {
320	            ffi::glm52_fp8_weight_only_gemv_partials_cuda(
321	                act_ptr as *const ffi::Half,
322	                w_ptr as *const u8,
323	                s_ptr as *const f32,
324	                out_ptr as *mut ffi::Half,
325	                scr_ptr,
326	                scr_floats,
327	                rows as i32,
328	                n as i32,
329	                k as i32,
330	                ctx.stream.cu_stream(),
331	                ksplit,
332	            )
333	        },
334	    }
335	    .result()
336	    .map_err(|err| anyhow!("GLM5.2 linear GEMV launch failed for rows={rows}, n={n}, k={k}: {err}"))
337	}
